current_answer: NLnet Restack is open to individuals for technical open-source projects, but an open form is not worldwide eligibility. The first call closes 3 November 2026 at 12:00 CET. A first grant request may be EUR 5,000–50,000. For this EU-funded programme, a clear European dimension is an eligibility gate: NLnet says it concerns the people doing the work, not merely users or benefits in Europe. Check the issuer’s current country guidance and name the contributing team before preparing the budget. Applicants outside the listed countries need a convincing case; NLnet decides fit and award. AI-topic and GenAI-use rules also apply.

catalogue_card.question: Can an individual outside the EU apply to NLnet Restack?
catalogue_card.text: Possibly, but the 3 November call is not an unrestricted global grant. NLnet checks the people contributing to the project and the European dimension before scoring it. Check your country against its current list and explain the team and budget; EU users alone are not enough.

summary: NLnet Restack accepts individuals for technical open-source projects and lists a 3 November 2026, 12:00 CET cutoff.
A first proposal may request EUR 5,000–50,000; the range is not an award promise.
European dimension concerns contributors, not just beneficiaries; country and team fit require the funder’s review.
uncertainty: Country classification, team composition and European-dimension fit require NLnet review; a project that benefits EU users alone is not enough.
The current GenAI policy applies, but NLnet says a revision is forthcoming.
A published first-grant range is a request range, not an award or a promise of selection.
